title: England call up Pope and Lawrence for the first two Tests against Pakistan
seoTitle: England name Pope, Lawrence for first two Tests vs Pak
subtitle: The Surrey duo returns to England's squad as Bethell is left out
excerpt: Surrey pair Ollie Pope and Dan Lawrence are back in England's squad for the first two Tests against Pakistan, while Bethell is omitted.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
England's cricket team announced the return of two Surrey players, Ollie Pope and Dan Lawrence, to the squad for the first two Tests against Pakistan. The decision underscores the technical directorate's choice to rely on the experience of these athletes in the matches that will kick off the series.

Call-up of Pope and Lawrence

Ollie Pope and Dan Lawrence, both attached to Surrey, were again included in the pool of players eligible to represent England in the Test matches. Their presence reinforces the strategy of maintaining a core of athletes who have already performed on the international stage, providing continuity to the team's performance.

Exclusion of Bethell

At the same time, the call-up omitted Bethell, who will not be part of the group for the first two Tests against Pakistan. The player's absence reflects a decision by the coaching staff that favors other options for the squad.

Context of the Test series

Tests are cricket's longest format, played over five days, and constitute the premier competition format among national sides. Each team fields a group of players that can vary according to the strategy adopted for each match, and call-ups are reviewed periodically to meet the tactical and physical demands of the athletes.

With Pope and Lawrence back in the group, England aims to balance the experience of players already tested at the international level with the need to adapt the squad to the specific conditions of the series against Pakistan.

With information from BBC Sport.
